title: CRISPR Technology in Biotechnology
text: Beyond its applications in basic research, CRISPR-Cas9 has been applied in agriculture to develop disease-resistant and drought-tolerant crops, in therapeutics to develop treatments for sickle cell disease and other genetic disorders, and in diagnostics (SHERLOCK, DETECTR platforms for pathogen detection). In 2023, the FDA approved the first CRISPR-based therapy, Casgevy, developed by Vertex Pharmaceuticals and CRISPR Therapeutics, to treat sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia. CRISPR has also been explored for potential applications in eradicating mosquito-borne diseases through gene drives. The technology continues to evolve with variants including base editing and prime editing that make more precise genetic changes.
